_comment: Ground truth for the outstanding-items scenarios on the synthetic baseline mailbox, corpus threads 46-74 and 120-124 (indexer/tests/baseline/corpus.py). Keyed by scenario id in agent_scenarios.json; an answering agent is given only the scenario's question, never this file. Evaluation date 2026-10-05, America/New_York: the window opens 2026-01-01T00:00:00-05:00, so t65.1 (sent 2025-12-31 21:30 -0500, which is 2026-01-01 02:30 UTC) is outside it. Message refs 'tNN.M' mean 'tNN.M@baseline.example'. Each action is a next action, scored by tests/agent_metrics.py: owner is one of avery_cole, blair_reed, sasha_ortiz, emery_vance, jordan, coordinator, jordan_or_coordinator, unknown; status is open, waiting (on someone other than the vendor), disputed, unknown (outstanding) or closed (to be excluded); due is the ISO date the mail supports, or null when it supports none; required_sources are the messages a conclusion must cite (any one); superseded_sources never support it; known_loss names the issue under which the tools cannot return the action's evidence; claims maps each claim kind the question or the mail makes relevant (sent, received, done; a kind left out is inapplicable) to its supported label (confirmed, proposed or unverified) and its proof set, sources: for sent the message in Sent, for received only an explicit acknowledgement of that transmission, for done the completion evidence, and none when the label is unverified. forbidden_sources may not be cited (identity decoy, prompt injection, mail outside the window); completeness_blockers must be named as limitations and forbid a completeness claim; full_read_messages must be paged through get_message to the end. evidence lists the decisive passage of each source (excerpt, whitespace-normalized) and, measured on the built baseline, which layers hold it: raw (the .eml's text parts), thread_text (threads.body_text, the thread FTS input: 2,000 characters per message, 4,000 tokens per thread), chunks (message_chunks), get_message (every body page), get_thread (every page, each body cut at 4,000 characters) and, for attachments, get_evidence (thread-scoped, with query) and search_attachments (with query). tests/baseline/test_outstanding_items_baseline.py checks these against the index. corpus_evidence lists, in the same shape, decisive passages of corpus shapes outside any scenario (#907: t89.1's sentence past the build's lowered extracted-characters cap; #908: t91.1's scanned page past the build's lowered OCR page cap; #1113: t92.1's TIFF frame past the same cap); no scenario or scorer reads it.

corpus_evidence._comment: #908: the third page of a scanned PDF, past the build's lowered OCR page cap (2). The page is an image, so no text part of the .eml holds the words (raw is false, hence lost_at raw) and OCR never reads it.

#1113: the third frame of a multipage TIFF, past the build's lowered OCR page cap (2), which the image OCR extractor applies frame by frame and logs when a frame is left unread (#885). The frame is an image, so no text part of the .eml holds the words (raw is false, hence lost_at raw) and OCR never reads it.
